_path_note: A = Aegis conversational intake (aegis_conversational_intake_v9.md). B = External LLM intake (aegis_llm_intake_v9.md). Both paths produce this schema. The Builder cannot distinguish which path was used.
_for_llm: Read aegis_llm_intake_v9.md fully before populating any field. This schema feeds an autonomous AI trading pipeline. What you write here directly determines what strategies are built and deployed with real capital.
_builder_note: Tier 1 (mandate_hard_constraints) fields are mathematical gates enforced by pipeline code. All other fields are investment policy context — read as a portfolio manager reads a client brief. mandate_priority_hierarchy is the conflict resolution profile — consult it whenever preferences trade off against each other.

mandate_hard_constraints._note: All fields enforced mechanically. No AI agent can override. Populate only from explicit user statements. Conservative interpretation always.

mandate_priority_hierarchy._builder_note: This section governs all trade-off decisions. When preferences conflict, the ordered_priorities ranking determines which preference yields. preference_flexibility tags tell you how hard each preference is — immovable preferences hold even at significant cost to other dimensions. trade_off_philosophy is the catch-all for conflicts the structured fields don't cover. Read this section before making any strategy generation decision that requires choosing between preferences.

investor_profile._builder_note: Read this section first. It calibrates how to interpret all subsequent fields — the user's sophistication, their relationship with markets, and what role this pipeline plays in their total investment picture.

risk_profile._builder_note: Risk is multi-dimensional. Do not reduce this section to a single label when building strategies. Each sub-field may produce different calibration decisions for different strategy types. regret_asymmetry has the largest single impact on exit rule design — weight it heavily.

performance_targets._builder_note: Use primary_objective as the anchor. Prose fields explain what the numbers mean to this user — a 20% return target from a consistency-prioritizing user is a fundamentally different mandate than the same target from one comfortable with drawdowns to achieve it. success_definition and failure_definition are the most actionable fields — they tell you what the user will actually do in real situations.

universe_mandate._builder_note: raw_desire is the primary signal — always read it first. universe_description gives dimensional context behind the hard filters. fundamental_screens is new in v9 — it captures financial characteristic requirements and interacts directly with the priority system. A fundamental_screens preference marked immovable in preference_flexibility is a hard filter even if it isn't in mandate_hard_constraints.

strategy_intent._builder_note: regime_universe_pairs are the most specific strategy generation signal — only create them from explicitly linked user preferences. regime_preferences describes the broader character without that specificity. exit_philosophy and entry_philosophy are high-signal — experienced investors often have strong views here that should be respected over system defaults.

horizon_mandate._builder_note: The hard horizon_allocation provides weights. This section explains the reasoning behind each bucket and what success looks like within each time frame. intraday_tolerance and overnight_tolerance are operationally critical — they determine what execution the user can actually perform.

portfolio_scope._builder_note: ambition_description calibrates how wide to cast the exploratory net. A narrow focused mandate and a broad diversified mandate require fundamentally different generation approaches. market_beta_intent interacts with portfolio_beta_existing — together they define what kind of exposure Aegis should add.

market_context._builder_note: macro_views bias regime and sector selection. strategy_implication within each view is Builder-actionable language — use it directly. current_regime_beliefs tells you what environment the user thinks the pipeline is being deployed into, which affects scenario selection for backtesting and validation.

execution_profile._builder_note: available_windows is a hard operational filter on strategy types — not a soft preference. A strategy that requires execution outside the user's windows will never be acted on and should not be generated. execution_latency_context affects entry range design — a user with 2-hour latency needs wider entry windows than one who can act in 10 minutes.

exclusions_and_constraints._builder_note: strategy_type_exclusions and tax_considerations are often the most actionable fields here. Always include the reason for each exclusion — the reason tells the Builder how firm the exclusion is and whether edge cases should be surfaced to the user.

filing_notes._builder_note: Read this section last, after reading the full schema. contradictions and expectation_corrections are surfaced to the user at confirmation. open_questions flag areas where conservative defaults should apply. conversation_quality_note tells you how much weight to give the full context vs. applying defaults.
